# Read-Write Model Instructions

Use these instructions when the material concerns handwriting, reading, writing, AI projection, re-entry, revision, drift, anchoring, or training the human model.

## Required Analysis

- Identify the loop stage: inscription, projection, re-entry, revision, drift control.
- Tag Book Part: Orientation / Grammar / Circuits / Futures.
- Tag EML Layer: Structural / Cognitive-Temporal / Agentic.
- Preserve any distinctive phrases.
- Name whether the output is source, study, asset, lexicon, or book draft.

## Placement

| Output | Save location |
| --- | --- |
| Focused study | `03-Working/Read-Write-Model/` |
| Step output | `03-Working/Step-*` |
| Stable definition | `06-Lexicon/Definitions/` |
| Diagram brief | `05-Assets/Diagrams/` |
| Circuit | `05-Assets/Circuits/` |
| Reading | `05-Assets/Readings/` |
| Book prose | `04-Book/Part-02-Grammar/` or `04-Book/Part-03-Circuits/` |

## Quality Bar

The Read-Write Model must remain practical and embodied. Do not let it become only an abstract theory. It should always be traceable to a page, a tool interaction, a classroom circuit, a diagram, or a return to handwriting.
